correctness.rationale: For exactly the graph GP(12,5) with 24 labelled vertices and 36 undirected edges, independently construct its edges u_i u_{i+1}, v_i v_{i+5}, u_i v_i and recursively enumerate all 120 perfect matchings. An anti-forcing S disjoint from M is equivalent to a hitting set for every N\M with N another perfect matching; any missing hit permits a competing perfect matching in G\S and every hit destroys all competitors. Independently enumerate all 144 graph automorphisms and partition the 120 matchings into eight orbits of sizes 3,6,36,18,12,24,18,3 (corresponding to the claimed table's ordering). For one representative of each, a separately implemented exhaustive hitting-set engine tests each subset of the 24 external edges in increasing cardinality until the first attainable degree, counts every minimizer and checks the eight profiles: (tau,orb,af,b) = ((6,6,6,6),3,8,1092), ((6,18),12,6,207), ((6,18),24,6,24), ((8,8,8),6,5,36), ((8,16),18,6,28), ((10,14),36,6,176), ((12,12),3,6,60), ((24),18,7,640). Automorphisms transfer af and b and the represented set covers all 120 matchings. Thus A_G(t)=6t^5+93t^6+18t^7+3t^8, sum_M b(M)=25,092, with (6,18) giving b=207 and 24 although af=6 in both. This is *genuinely exhaustive finite proof* conditional on the explicitly specified complete enumeration/hitting algorithm and automorphism logic, not extrapolation or unverified solver output. Original 87k source certificate additionally provides alternating-cycle bounds, but independent verification used an alternative full enumeration.

value.rationale: The complete anti-forcing polynomial and the refined distribution by 2-factor cycle structure on the canonical, highly symmetric cubic bipartite Nauru graph are motivated exact graph invariants. The unexpected split of two distinct (6,18) orbits with identical af but different minimizer multiplicities shows that cycle-length partition is insufficient to determine the refined optimum count; this structural observation is not reproduced by elementary forcing-number bounds. A full finite classification is valuable without an infinite family theorem.
